title: The courtyard gate
bodyMd:
In a fictional housing block, a courtyard had long been described as unused. The management proposed converting it into parking spaces. Before approving the change, residents observed the courtyard at different times. Children played there after school, a caretaker sorted deliveries there early in the morning, and several older residents sat in its shade during summer afternoons. None of these activities appeared in the original survey, which had been conducted at midday in winter.

The observations did not show that parking was unnecessary. They showed that the comparison had been framed incorrectly: the choice was not between parking and an empty space, but between parking and several existing uses. The residents requested a proposal that counted those uses and investigated alternatives. In their view, recognizing an activity did not automatically settle its priority, but failing to recognize it prevented a fair discussion.
